clips.send: Personal freedom. The textbook calls personal freedom the most basic and most important right of a citizen. Freedom of the person: no one may be arrested except with the approval or decision of a procuratorate, or the decision of a court, and the arrest must be made by the police. Personal dignity: your name, your image, your reputation and your privacy are protected by law. Your home may not be unlawfully searched or entered. Freedom and privacy of correspondence: your letters and messages are protected by law.

clips.send: A citizen’s basic duties. Duties set by law must be carried out. Obey the Constitution and the laws (and keep state secrets, protect public property, keep public order, respect social morality). Safeguard the country’s interests: its unity, the unity of all its ethnic groups, and its security, honour and interests. Perform military service according to law — the Constitution calls it an honourable duty. Pay taxes according to law — taxes are “taken from the people and used for the people”.

clips.send: Political rights and freedoms. The rights that let citizens take part in the country’s political life. Voting and standing for election: every citizen aged 18 or over, whatever their ethnic group, sex, job, family background, religion, education, property or length of residence (except people the law has deprived of political rights). Political freedoms: speech, the press, assembly, association, procession and demonstration. The right to supervise (监督权): citizens may criticise and make suggestions to any state organ or official, and may report officials who break the law.

clips.send: Social, economic, cultural and educational rights. The rights that protect a citizen’s living, working and learning. Property: a citizen’s lawful private property may not be violated — you may own, use, benefit from and dispose of it, and inherit. Material help (物质帮助权): citizens who are old, ill or unable to work have the right to help from the state and society. Work and education belong here too — and they are also duties (see the “both” bar). Citizens are free to do scientific research, create literature and art, and take part in other cultural activities.

clips.send: Rights and duties go together. A citizen both enjoys lawful rights and bears legal duties. The Constitution: every citizen enjoys the rights and must at the same time perform the duties it and the laws set out. Rights and duties depend on and strengthen each other. “No rights without duties, and no duties without rights.”. So: use your rights lawfully and carry out your duties willingly.

clips.send: How to defend a right. When a right is harmed, defend it through lawful steps. 1, Negotiate (协商): talk it out directly with the other side. 2, Mediation (调解): a neutral third party, such as a people’s mediation committee, helps both sides agree. 3, Arbitration (仲裁): an arbitration body gives a binding decision. 4, Lawsuit (诉讼): go to court. The textbook calls it the most formal and authoritative way — “the last line of defence”.

clips.send: Rights have limits. Citizens may not go beyond a right’s limits or abuse it. When using their freedoms and rights, citizens may not harm the interests of the state, of society or of the collective, or the lawful freedoms and rights of other citizens. Rights must be used in the way the law provides (lawful procedure). Example: freedom of speech does not cover insulting people or spreading rumours online.

clips.send: Work and education: both. “Citizens have the right as well as the duty to work” and “to receive education”. Education as a right: the state must provide schools; no one may stop a child from attending. Education as a duty: school-age children must attend and finish the nine years of compulsory education. Work as a right: citizens with the ability to work may have a job and be paid for it. Work as a duty: working is how citizens support themselves and contribute to society.

clips.send: 维权的途径。公民权利受到损害，要依照法定程序维权。一、协商：当事人直接沟通，自行解决。二、调解：在人民调解委员会等第三方主持下达成协议。三、仲裁：由仲裁机构依法作出裁决。四、诉讼：向人民法院起诉。诉讼是处理纠纷和应对侵害最正规、最权威的手段，是维护合法权益的最后屏障。

clips.send: 政治权利和自由。公民依法参与国家政治生活、管理国家事务的权利和自由。选举权和被选举权：年满18周岁的公民，不分民族、种族、性别、职业、家庭出身、宗教信仰、教育程度、财产状况、居住期限，都有选举权和被选举权（依照法律被剥夺政治权利的人除外）。政治自由：公民有言论、出版、集会、结社、游行、示威的自由。监督权：公民对任何国家机关和国家工作人员有提出批评和建议的权利；对其违法失职行为，有申诉、控告或者检举的权利。

clips.send: 人身自由。人身自由是公民最基本、最重要的权利。人身自由不受侵犯：任何公民，非经人民检察院批准或者决定或者人民法院决定，并由公安机关执行，不受逮捕。人格尊严不受侵犯：公民享有姓名权、肖像权、名誉权、荣誉权、隐私权等。住宅不受侵犯：禁止非法搜查或者非法侵入公民的住宅。通信自由和通信秘密受法律保护。

clips.send: 社会经济与文化教育权利。保障公民生活、劳动和学习的权利。财产权：公民的合法的私有财产不受侵犯；公民依法对自己的财产享有占有、使用、收益、处分的权利，并享有继承权。物质帮助权：公民在年老、疾病或者丧失劳动能力的情况下，有从国家和社会获得物质帮助的权利。劳动权和受教育权也属于这一类——它们同时又是义务。公民有进行科学研究、文学艺术创作和其他文化活动的自由。

clips.send: 劳动、受教育：既是权利又是义务。我国宪法规定：公民有劳动的权利和义务；公民有受教育的权利和义务。受教育是权利：国家举办学校、保障适龄儿童少年入学，任何人不得剥夺其受教育的机会。受教育是义务：适龄儿童、少年必须按时入学，完成九年义务教育。劳动是权利：有劳动能力的公民有获得工作和取得劳动报酬的权利。劳动是义务：劳动是一切有劳动能力的公民的光荣职责。

clips.send: 行使权利有界限。公民行使权利不能超越它本身的界限，不能滥用权利。公民在行使自由和权利的时候，不得损害国家的、社会的、集体的利益和其他公民的合法的自由和权利。公民行使权利应依照法定程序，按照规定的活动方式、步骤和过程。例如：言论自由不包括侮辱、诽谤他人或在网上散布谣言。

clips.send: 公民的基本义务。法定义务须履行：法律要求做的必须去做，法律禁止做的坚决不做。遵守宪法和法律（保守国家秘密，爱护公共财产，遵守劳动纪律，遵守公共秩序，尊重社会公德）。维护国家利益：维护国家统一和全国各民族团结；维护祖国的安全、荣誉和利益。依法服兵役：保卫祖国、抵抗侵略是每一个公民的神圣职责；依照法律服兵役和参加民兵组织是公民的光荣义务。依法纳税：我国税收取之于民、用之于民。

clips.send: 权利和义务相统一。公民既是合法权利的享有者，又是法定义务的承担者。宪法规定：任何公民享有宪法和法律规定的权利，同时必须履行宪法和法律规定的义务。公民的权利和义务相互依存、相互促进。没有无义务的权利，也没有无权利的义务。我们要坚持权利和义务相统一：依法行使权利，自觉履行义务。
